Leonardo, this is Claire Ashworth, head of compliance at Northgate Pay. I have just read the bulletin your team sent, and I need something much shorter for my board. They will not read four pages. What I need is three lines. What was changed, what is now required of us, and what is still open. Two things worry me. The first is the beneficial ownership rule, because our onboarding was built for the old regime, and I am told that nothing was announced before the text was published. The second is the withholding rate. Fifteen percent is a lot of cash, and if we can be held liable for a mistake made by a partner bank, my board will want that in writing. One more thing, and please do not take it personally. Do not send me another document full of by whom and by which. Tell me what happens, and tell me who has to act on Monday morning. Thank you.

Something I learned late, and I wish somebody had told me at your stage. In this profession the passive is not decoration. It is a decision. When you write that a penalty was imposed, you are choosing not to name who imposed it, and nine times out of ten that is the right call, because the client does not care and the sentence is cleaner. But the same habit becomes a real problem in the last paragraph of a memo. If your recommendation says that the documents should be reviewed and the exposure has been assessed, nobody in that company knows who is supposed to do anything on Monday morning. So here is the rule I use, and it has never failed me. Describe the regulation in the passive. Describe the action in the active. The rules were changed, the deadline was moved, the penalty was raised. And then, in the last three lines, your team files the return, we prepare the ruling request, you sign by the twentieth.

Let me summarize what has been changed this quarter. The reporting framework was enacted in December, and the first stage is already in force. Two new obligations are imposed on financial institutions this year. Nothing has been decided about the old credit, so we wait for the September bulletin.
